examples.en: He was called a turncoat by his colleagues.
It's not easy to forgive a turncoat.
We learned a story about a turncoat in history class.
In the movie, the turncoat regrets it at the end.
Nobody believed the turncoat's words.
The word 'turncoat' is a very heavy expression.

explain: 원래 편을 배신하고 돌아선 사람을 강하게 비난하는 말이에요. 일상에서 친구를 가볍게 '배신자'라고 놀리는 것과 달리, 정치나 역사 이야기에서 무겁게 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 그 작가는 변절자로 불리며 비난을 받았어요.
phrases.en: The writer was called a turncoat and criticized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비난하는 이름으로 불린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being given a name of blame.

phrases.en: People condemned him as a turncoat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-라고'를 붙여 어떤 말로 비난하는지 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -라고 shows what label is used to criticize.

phrases.example: 친구를 두고 혼자 떠난 그를 배신자라고 생각했어요.
phrases.en: I thought of him as a traitor for leaving his friend behind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변절자'보다 일상에서 더 널리 쓰고 가벼운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more widely in daily life and lighter than 변절자.

explain_en: This is a strong word of condemnation for someone who betrayed their side and turned away. Unlike lightly teasing a friend as a '배신자' (traitor) in daily life, it is used heavily in politics and history.

en: blessing; someone or something that brings good fortune

examples.en: Our youngest is the family's bundle of good luck.

examples.ko: 아기가 태어난 뒤로 일이 잘 풀려서 복덩어리라고 불러요.
examples.en: Things went well after the baby was born, so we call him our lucky charm.

examples.ko: 이 강아지는 우리 집에 온 복덩어리가 틀림없어요.
examples.en: This puppy must be a blessing that came to our home.
The new employee seems like a real stroke of luck.
I'm happy that such a blessing of a daughter-in-law joined the family.
I came home from the hospital holding our little bundle of luck.

explain: 집이나 모임에 들어와 좋은 일을 가져다주는 사람에게 애정을 담아 쓰는 말이에요. 아기, 새 식구, 새 직원에게 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '복덩이'도 있어요.

phrases.en: Our puppy is the lucky charm of the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이고 더 짧고 정겨워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that is shorter and warmer.

phrases.example: 새로 온 직원이 우리 팀의 복덩어리예요.
phrases.en: The new employee is a blessing to our team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 쓰는 해요체 모양이에요. 애정을 담아 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite predicate form, said with affection.

phrases.en: The youngest is called the family's lucky charm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족을 가리킬 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing when referring to family members.

explain_en: Person, pet or thing that brings good luck to a family, casual. It is an affectionate word for someone who brings good fortune to a home or group. It is often used for babies, new family members and new coworkers. '복덩이' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 그 애는 새침데기라서 처음엔 말을 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: She's a bit aloof, so she doesn't talk much at first.

examples.ko: 새침데기처럼 굴더니 알고 보니 아주 다정해요.
examples.en: He acted all stuck-up, but it turns out he's very kind.

examples.ko: 우리 반 새침데기가 오늘 웃는 걸 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw our class's aloof girl smile for the first time today.

examples.ko: 내 동생은 새침데기지만 친구들에게 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: My younger sister is a bit prim, but she's popular with her friends.
The aloof cat doesn't like being petted.
People mistake her for a snob.

explain: 쌀쌀맞게 보이거나 도도한 척하는 사람을 조금 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요. 주로 여자아이나 여자에게 많이 쓰고, 친한 사이에서는 귀엽게 말할 수 있지만 모르는 사람에게는 실례가 될 수 있어요. '깍쟁이'와 비슷하지만 '깍쟁이'에는 인색하다는 뜻도 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 애는 새침데기 같지만 말해 보면 친절해요.
phrases.en: She seems aloof, but she's kind when you talk to her.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 쌀쌀맞아 보일 때 '같다'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '같다' when someone's appearance seems cold.

phrases.example: 새침데기 고양이가 나를 쳐다보고 안 와요.
phrases.en: The aloof cat looks at me and doesn't come over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도도해 보이는 동물에게 귀엽게 쓸 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used cutely for animals that act aloof.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 깍쟁이 같아서 처음엔 가까워지기 어려웠어요.
phrases.en: That friend seemed a bit prim, so it was hard to get close at first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하게 사람을 놀리듯 부르는 말이지만 '새침데기'보다 야무지고 얄미운 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar teasing word, but with a shrewder, slightly annoying feel compared with '새침데기'.

explain_en: It teasingly names someone who seems cool and standoffish. It is used mostly for girls and women; among close people it can sound cute, but to strangers it can be rude. It is similar to '깍쟁이', but '깍쟁이' can also mean stingy.

en: to place confidence in; to trust with a task

examples.en: The boss trusts that employee a lot.
A teacher whom everyone trusts has newly arrived.

examples.ko: 팀장님이 저를 신임해서 큰 일을 맡겼어요.
examples.en: My team leader trusted me and gave me a big job.

examples.ko: 국민이 신임한 대통령이라도 실수를 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a president the people trusted can make mistakes.

examples.ko: 저를 신임하지 않으면 이 일은 못 해요.
examples.en: If you do not trust me, I cannot do this job.

examples.ko: 앞으로도 신임할 수 있는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be someone people can trust from now on.

explain: '신임하다'는 사람의 능력을 믿고 일을 맡긴다는 느낌이라서 직장이나 조직 이야기에 많이 나와요. 친구를 믿을 때는 '믿다'를 쓰고, 마음을 놓는 느낌일 때는 '신뢰하다'가 더 가까워요. '신임을 얻다', '신임을 받다'처럼 명사 '신임'과도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그 직원은 일을 잘해서 사장님의 신임을 얻었어요.
phrases.en: That employee did well and gained the boss's trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신임하다'의 명사형 '신임'과 함께 써서 믿음을 받는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 신임 to talk about earning someone's confidence.

phrases.en: I don't have confidence in that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 일을 맡길 만큼 믿지 못한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means not trusting someone enough to rely on them.

phrases.en: The team leader is trusted by all the staff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿음을 받는 쪽에서 말하는 표현으로 직장에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person being trusted, common at work.

explain_en: A superior trusts you and assigns an important task. 신임하다 has the feeling of trusting someone's ability enough to give them work, so it shows up in workplace and organization talk. For a friend you use 믿다, and 신뢰하다 is closer to relying with peace of mind. The noun also appears as 신임을 얻다 or 신임을 받다.

t90.ax: The boss trusts that employee a lot.

examples.ko: 교실 뒤에서 친구들이 쑥덕쑥덕 이야기하고 있어요.
examples.en: My friends are whispering at the back of the classroom.

examples.ko: 제가 들어가자 사람들이 쑥덕쑥덕 말하다가 갑자기 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: When I walked in, people were whispering and then suddenly went quiet.
The neighborhood ladies are whispering rumors to each other.
What are you two whispering about so secretly?

examples.ko: 회의 중에 뒤에서 쑥덕쑥덕하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear whispering from behind during the meeting.

examples.ko: 아이들이 선물을 숨기고 쑥덕쑥덕 작전을 짜요.
examples.en: The kids hide the present and whisper as they plan their scheme.

explain: 남이 들으면 안 되는 이야기나 소문, 흉을 작은 소리로 주고받는 느낌이 있어요. '속닥속닥', '수군수군'과 비슷하게 쓰는데, 뒷말하는 분위기일 때 특히 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: People are whispering behind my back as they look at me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쑥덕쑥덕'을 동사로 쓴 말로, 남의 이야기를 작은 소리로 주고받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 쑥덕쑥덕; it means to exchange whispered talk about someone.

phrases.example: 아이들이 책상 아래에서 속닥속닥 비밀 이야기를 해요.
phrases.en: The kids are whispering secrets under the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 흉보는 느낌이 덜하고, 비밀 이야기를 나누는 분위기에도 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but less like gossiping; it also fits sharing secrets.

phrases.en: Employees are murmuring in front of the meeting room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 낮은 소리로 소문 같은 이야기를 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when several people talk in low voices, as if sharing rumors.

explain_en: It carries the feel of exchanging quiet talk, rumors or gossip that others shouldn't hear. It is close to '속닥속닥' and '수군수군', and fits especially well when the mood is one of talking behind someone's back.

t90.ax: What are you two whispering about so secretly?

examples.en: I'm still a greenhorn, so I lack experience.
The seniors still treat me like a kid.
I heard that rookie already won the competition.

examples.ko: 애송이 시절에는 실수도 정말 많이 했어요.
examples.en: In my greenhorn days, I made so many mistakes.
Don't act like a kid; take some responsibility.
They looked down on him as a rookie and ended up losing the match.

explain: 나이가 어리거나 경험이 적은 사람을 약간 낮추어 부르는 말이에요. '풋내기'와 비슷하고, 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 쓰거나 자기 자신을 낮출 때 써요. 처음 본 사람에게 쓰면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I'm still a greenhorn at this job.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애송이'와 비슷하지만 조금 덜 낮추는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'aesongi', but feels a little less belittling.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 아직 애송이 같아 보여요.
phrases.en: That person still seems like a rookie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어리고 미숙해 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks young and inexperienced.

phrases.en: I made many mistakes back when I was a rookie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험이 적었던 때를 돌아보며 자기 자신에게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used about yourself when looking back on your inexperienced days.

explain_en: Belittling, spoken; a young, inexperienced person (형은 저를 아직 애송이라고 놀리곤 해요.) It is a slightly belittling word for someone young or inexperienced. It is similar to '풋내기', and is used by a senior toward a junior, or when people put themselves down. Using it on someone you've just met can sound insulting.

t90.ax: The seniors still treat me like a kid.

examples.en: He is a famous linguist who studies Korean.

examples.ko: 언어학자가 되려면 대학에서 언어학을 공부해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a linguist, you have to study linguistics at university.
The class taught by the professor, who is a linguist, is the most fun.
Linguists observe how language changes.
I've dreamed of becoming a linguist since I was little.

examples.ko: 언어학자의 설명을 들으니 문법이 쉽게 이해됐어요.
examples.en: After hearing the linguist's explanation, I understood the grammar easily.

explain: 외국어를 잘하는 사람이나 통역사와는 달라요. 언어 자체의 구조나 변화를 연구하는 사람을 말해요. 그래서 여러 언어를 못해도 언어학자가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I want to become a linguist someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 진로를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used when talking about dreams or career goals.

phrases.en: That book was written by a famous linguist.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유명한'이 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 사람을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 유명한 describes the noun after it. Use it when introducing a person.

phrases.en: Linguists are studying new words.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙여 여러 명을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -들 makes it plural.

explain_en: This is different from someone who is good at foreign languages or an interpreter. A linguist studies the structure and change of language itself, so a person can be a linguist without speaking many languages.

examples.en: That person is no pushover.

examples.ko: 새로 온 팀장님이 여간내기가 아니라서 긴장돼요.
examples.en: The new team leader is formidable, so I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 저 가게 사장님은 여간내기가 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.en: That shop owner seems like no ordinary person.

examples.ko: 동생이 여간내기가 아니라서 아무도 못 속여요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is so sharp that nobody can fool them.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 여간내기는 아니니까 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: That player is no easy opponent, so we have to be careful.
I heard that she's quite a formidable person.

explain: 거의 '여간내기가 아니다'처럼 부정과 함께 써서, 만만치 않고 보통 사람과 다르다는 말이 돼요. 능력이 뛰어나서 감탄할 때도, 상대하기 까다로워서 경계할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The new teacher is no pushover.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보통 사람이 아니다'라는 말을 그대로 풀면 되지만, 실제로는 능력이 대단하거나 만만치 않다는 감탄·경계를 담은 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It literally says 'not an ordinary person', but in practice it is a set phrase carrying admiration or wariness about someone formidable.

explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '여간내기가 아니다', meaning someone is not to be underestimated. It can express admiration for someone's ability or wariness about someone hard to deal with.

en: to be clever; to be cunning; to be crafty

examples.ko: 그 아이는 나이는 어려도 정말 영악해요.
examples.en: That child is really shrewd even though he's young.
Be careful not to be fooled by a crafty merchant.

examples.ko: 동생이 영악하게 부모님께 용돈을 받아 냈어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling cleverly got pocket money out of our parents.
That friend is shrewd, but has a warm heart.

examples.ko: 영악해서 손해 보는 일은 절대 안 해요.
examples.en: He's so shrewd that he never does anything that costs him.

examples.ko: 영악했던 그 후배는 결국 먼저 승진했어요.
examples.en: That shrewd junior colleague ended up getting promoted first.

explain: 똑똑하다는 뜻이지만 '영악하다'는 자기에게 이익이 되게 꾀를 잘 쓴다는 느낌이 있어서 칭찬만으로 들리지 않을 때가 많아요. 순수하게 머리가 좋다고 칭찬할 때는 '영특하다'나 '똑똑하다'가 더 알맞아요.

phrases.example: 동생이 영악하게 행동해서 용돈을 더 받았어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling acted cunningly and got more pocket money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영악하게'는 자기에게 이익이 되도록 꾀를 쓴다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '영악하게' implies using tricks to benefit oneself.

phrases.en: That child's eyes look sly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에서 꾀가 많아 보인다는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gives the impression of being crafty.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 꾀가 많아서 숙제를 잘 피해요.
phrases.en: That child is full of tricks and avoids homework well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영악하다'와 비슷하지만 더 가볍고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '영악하다' but lighter and more everyday.

explain_en: Smart in a self-serving way; often said of kids, slightly negative. It means smart, but '영악하다' suggests using tricks to benefit oneself, so it often doesn't sound like pure praise. To simply praise someone's brains, '영특하다' or '똑똑하다' fits better.

t90.ax: That friend is shrewd, but has a warm heart.

en: by nature; just like; born to be

examples.ko: 그 친구는 천생 예술가라서 늘 그림을 그려요.
examples.en: My friend is a born artist, so he's always drawing.

examples.ko: 선생님은 천생 교사라서 쉬는 날에도 학생 걱정을 하세요.
examples.en: Our teacher is a natural-born teacher and worries about students even on days off.

examples.ko: 그 사람, 천생 어린아이 같아서 미워할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: He's just like a child by nature, so I can't hate him.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 취향이 똑같아서 천생연분이라고 해요.
examples.en: The two have identical tastes, so people call them a perfect match.

examples.ko: 싸운 적도 없이 십 년을 산다니 천생연분이 따로 없네요.
examples.en: Ten years together without a single fight? They're truly meant for each other.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 천생 농사꾼이라 은퇴하고도 밭에 나가세요.
examples.en: Grandpa is a born farmer, so he still goes to the field after retiring.

explain: '천생 ○○이다'처럼 뒤에 직업이나 성격을 나타내는 명사가 와서, 그 모습이 몸에 밴 듯 타고났다는 느낌을 줘요. 칭찬일 때도, 어쩔 수 없다는 뉘앙스일 때도 있어요. '천생연분'은 이 말이 들어간 굳은 표현으로 부부나 연인에게 많이 써요.

phrases.en: That couple is a perfect match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하늘이 맺어 준 것처럼 잘 맞는 인연을 말해요. 부부나 연인에게 쓰는 좋은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a pairing so fitting it seems arranged by heaven. It is a warm compliment for couples.

explain_en: It is followed by a noun for a job or personality, as in '천생 ○○이다', giving the feel that someone is that way by nature. It can be praise or a shrug that it can't be helped. '천생연분' is a fixed expression built on it, often used for couples.

examples.en: My older sister is a cellist who works in an orchestra.
I cried after hearing the cellist play.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 첼리스트가 되는 게 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, my dream was to become a cellist.

examples.ko: 그 첼리스트는 공연 때마다 같은 곡을 연주해요.
examples.en: That cellist plays the same piece at every concert.
I want to learn the cello from a cellist.
The cellists came on stage and took their seats.

explain: 악기 이름 뒤에 '-리스트/-니스트'가 붙은 직업 이름이에요. '바이올리니스트', '피아니스트'처럼 말해요. 악기는 '첼로'이고 '첼로 연주자'라고 풀어서 말할 수도 있어요.

phrases.example: 저는 어른이 되면 첼리스트가 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: When I grow up, I want to become a cellist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when talking about dreams or careers.

phrases.en: He is a famous cello player.
phrases.nuance_ko: '첼리스트'를 풀어서 말한 표현으로, 더 쉽고 설명하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out version of 'cellist', plain and descriptive.

phrases.en: He works as a cellist in Germany.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 '-(으)로 일하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-(으)로 일하다' to state someone's job.

explain_en: This is a job name formed by adding a '-리스트/-니스트' ending to an instrument, like '바이올리니스트' and '피아니스트'. The instrument is '첼로', and you can also say '첼로 연주자' (cello player).

en: to be loyal; to be devoted

examples.en: Our dog is really loyal.
That retainer was a loyal man to the king.

examples.ko: 충성스러운 친구가 한 명만 있어도 든든해요.
examples.en: Even one loyal friend is reassuring.
He worked devotedly and was recognized by the boss.
The loyal subordinate stayed to the very end.

examples.ko: 이 경찰견은 충성스러워서 주인을 잘 따라요.
examples.en: This police dog is loyal, so it follows its owner well.

explain: 윗사람, 나라, 주인에게 마음을 다하는 모습에 써요. 개 같은 동물에게 칭찬으로도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 윗사람을 잘 따른다는 느낌이 강해요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '충성스러워요', '충성스러운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: That dog is famous for being loyal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이고 동물에게 칭찬으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, often used as praise for animals.

phrases.en: That employee really looks loyal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 보이는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an impression based on how someone appears.

phrases.en: That person is not very loyal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이라 충성하는 느낌이 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning there is no sense of loyalty.

explain_en: Adjective describing someone as loyal by nature or character; focuses on the trait (충성스러운 신하). Use it for wholehearted devotion to a superior, a country, or an owner. It is also used as praise for animals such as dogs. Said about a person, it carries a strong sense of following a superior well. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it becomes '충성스러워요' and '충성스러운'.

en: to admonish; to lecture; to caution

examples.en: The teacher quietly admonished the student who was late.

examples.ko: 부모님은 아이를 너무 심하게 훈계하지 않아요.
examples.en: My parents don't lecture the child too harshly.

examples.ko: 사람들 앞에서 후배를 훈계하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't lecture a junior in front of other people.
Grandfather always lectures us to be polite.
Even when I lecture him, the child only pretends to listen.

examples.ko: 그는 친구를 훈계할 만큼 잘난 사람이 아니에요.
examples.en: He is not a person who is good enough to lecture his friends.

explain: 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 잘못을 고치라고 타이를 때 쓰는 말이라, 친구 사이에는 어색해요. 친구에게는 '충고하다'가 자연스럽고, '타이르다'는 더 부드러운 느낌이에요. 훈계 내용이 맞더라도 말투가 길어지면 '잔소리'로 들려요.

phrases.en: The principal admonished the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 하는 일이라서 높임 '-시-'를 넣은 존댓말 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific '-시-' form, used because the admonisher is a superior.

phrases.en: A lecturing tone is uncomfortable to listen to.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 말투나 태도를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form modifies a tone or attitude.

phrases.en: Please don't lecture me so much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형으로 듣기 싫은 마음을 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to show you don't want to be lectured.

explain_en: Scold or advise someone about wrong behavior. This is for a senior person telling a junior to correct a mistake, so it sounds awkward between friends. With friends, '충고하다' is more natural, and '타이르다' feels gentler. Even when the content is right, a long lecturing tone gets heard as '잔소리' (nagging).

t90.ax: Grandfather always lectures us to be polite.

en: to advise; to urge; to recommend

examples.en: The doctor advised me to exercise.
The government urges people to wear masks indoors.

examples.ko: 회사에서 일찍 퇴근하라고 권고했는데도 다들 남았어요.
examples.en: The company urged everyone to leave early, but they all stayed.

examples.ko: 전문가들이 물을 자주 마시라고 권고하고 있어요.
examples.en: Experts recommend drinking water often.

examples.ko: 선생님이 한 번 쉬어 보라고 권고하셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher advised me to take a break.
The committee will recommend that the rule be changed.

explain: 권고하다는 정부, 의사, 기관이 '이렇게 하는 것이 좋다'고 공식적으로 말할 때 써요. 친구에게 추천할 때는 '추천하다'나 '권하다'를 써요. 강제는 아니라서 따르지 않아도 되지만 하는 편이 좋다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I followed the doctor's advice and quit drinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '권고'를 명사로 써서 그 말을 받아들인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '권고' as a noun to mean accepting that advice.

phrases.en: I was advised at the hospital to rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 권고를 듣는 쪽일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are the one receiving the advice.

phrases.en: My friend recommended this book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구 사이에서는 '권고하다'보다 '권하다'가 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than '권고하다' among friends.

explain_en: Formal advice from doctors, officials or institutions. 권고하다 is for governments, doctors or institutions officially saying that something is advisable. To a friend you would say 추천하다 or 권하다. It is not an order: you may ignore it, but it is better to follow.

dis.h: formal advice urging someone to act
gh: everyday: suggest something good, e.g., restaurant
urge or offer someone to take/do

p.n: 권하다 is softer and more everyday; 권고하다 sounds formal and official.

t90.ax: The doctor advised me to exercise.
